_doc: Tools Claude Code works faster with, read by scripts/toolcheck.py. tier: essential (offer to install when missing) | recommended (offer once, one list) | role (only when intake names that kind of work). bins: executable names to look for, first hit wins. install: package id per manager; null = not available there. why: one plain sentence shown to the person. claude_hint: one line written into the user-level CLAUDE.md so Claude uses the tool without probing for it.

winget.note: built into Windows 10/11; --scope user installs without admin for packages that support it

scoop.note: installs into the user folder, no admin; the usual route on a locked-down work laptop
scoop.bootstrap: Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope CurrentUser; irm get.scoop.sh | iex

brew.note: standard on Mac; installing brew itself needs admin once

tools.name: Git
tools.why: Tracks every change so mistakes can be undone; on Windows it also provides the Bash shell Claude Code uses.
tools.claude_hint: git is installed: check `git status` before and after edits; commit in small steps.

tools.name: Python 3
tools.why: Lets Claude write and run small scripts for data, files and spreadsheets instead of doing them by hand.
tools.claude_hint: Python 3 is installed (`{bin}`): prefer a short script over long shell pipelines for data and file work.

tools.name: Node.js (LTS)
tools.why: Runs web tooling and most add-on servers (MCP) that extend what Claude can reach.
tools.claude_hint: Node.js is installed: `npx` can run JS tooling without a global install.

tools.name: ripgrep
tools.why: Searches whole folders in a blink, so Claude finds things without reading every file.
tools.claude_hint: ripgrep is installed: use `rg` for shell searches instead of grep or Select-String.

tools.name: jq
tools.why: Reads and reshapes JSON (what most tools and APIs return) in one short command.
tools.claude_hint: jq is installed: slice JSON with `jq` instead of reading whole files.

tools.name: GitHub CLI
tools.why: Lets Claude open pull requests, read issues and check builds without the browser.
tools.claude_hint: GitHub CLI is installed: use `gh` for PRs, issues and CI status (`gh auth status` first).

tools.name: fd
tools.why: Finds files by name quickly, skipping clutter like build folders.
tools.claude_hint: fd is installed (`{bin}`): use it to find files by name.

tools.name: uv
tools.why: Installs Python packages and runs Python tools without admin rights or a tangled setup.
tools.claude_hint: uv is installed: use `uv run` / `uvx` for Python packages instead of global pip installs.

tools.name: Pandoc
tools.why: Converts between Word, Markdown, HTML and PDF so Claude can read and produce office documents.
tools.claude_hint: pandoc is installed: convert .docx to Markdown before reading, and back when delivering.

tools.name: Azure CLI
tools.why: Lets Claude inspect Azure resources you already have access to.
tools.claude_hint: Azure CLI is installed: read-only `az` queries are fine; ask before anything that changes resources.

tools.name: AWS CLI
tools.why: Lets Claude inspect AWS resources you already have access to.
tools.claude_hint: AWS CLI is installed: read-only `aws` queries are fine; ask before anything that changes resources.

tools.name: Docker
tools.why: Runs services in containers so Claude can build and test them locally.
tools.claude_hint: Docker is installed: prefer containers for services rather than installing them on the machine.

tools.name: .NET SDK
tools.claude_hint: .NET SDK is installed: `dotnet build` / `dotnet test` are the project checks.

tools.name: Java (JDK 21)
tools.claude_hint: A JDK is installed: use the project's wrapper (`./gradlew`, `./mvnw`) when there is one.
